name: manipulation
about: LEVI's built-in, task-agnostic vocabulary of manipulation subtasks. Every dataset starts from it unless it has a vocabulary of its own; an annotator may add a subtask it lacks (with the same fields) while annotating. Object-transfer phases come first -- they cover pick-and-place, stacking and most tabletop tasks -- then contact skills. Definitions name the observable onset: a boundary is where the defined event first happens, not where it becomes obvious. The task's own instruction states which objects and targets count and anything task-specific.
sources: RH20T-P primitive skills (Chen et al., 2024): pick includes the preparation, place includes release and withdrawal
AgiBot World atomic skills: pick, place, insert, pour, click, slide, push, pull, twist, press, open, close
BridgeData V2 skills (Walke et al., 2023): pick-and-place, push, reorient, open/close doors and drawers, wipe, fold, stack, twist knobs, flip switches, turn faucets, zip, sweep
DROID verb distribution (Khazatsky et al., 2024): 86 normalized verbs, most frequent pick, place, open, move, close
EPIC-KITCHENS-100 verb classes (Damen et al., 2022) and Rubicon Boundaries (Moltisanti et al., 2017): onset of the action, only the last preliminary motion
MimicGen (Mandlekar et al., 2023): object-centric subtasks, boundary at the step before contact
Round 1-8 plate-stacking experiment of LEVI: the attempt rule (built-in knowledge annotation-007)

subtasks.label: approach
subtasks.definition: The effector moves toward an object or place it is about to act on, without carrying it -- including the move from letting go of one object to the next contact.
subtasks.starts_when: The effector starts moving toward the object or place it will act on next.
subtasks.ends_when: The effector first touches the object (or reaches the place it will act at).
subtasks.success_when: The effector reaches the object.
subtasks.confusions: Only the last preliminary motion before the contact; a wander elsewhere first is other. Carrying an object toward a target is transport.

subtasks.label: grasp
subtasks.definition: The effector takes hold of an object: from first contact until the object moves with it. One attempt is one continuous engagement.
subtasks.starts_when: The fingers (or suction, or hand) first touch the object.
subtasks.ends_when: The object first moves with the effector -- or the effector lets go and leaves (a failed attempt).
subtasks.success_when: The object is held and lifted or moved with the effector.
subtasks.confusions: Re-closing or adjusting while staying on the object is the same attempt; letting go and leaving ends it, and the next touch is a new grasp after an approach. Failure when the effector leaves without the object.

subtasks.label: transport
subtasks.definition: A held object is carried from where it was to above or beside its target.
subtasks.starts_when: The held object leaves its support.
subtasks.ends_when: The object is above or at its target and starts being set down.
subtasks.success_when: The object reaches the intended target.
subtasks.confusions: Carrying toward the wrong target is failure. Moving an object without holding it is push or pull.

subtasks.label: place
subtasks.definition: A held object is lowered onto, into or against its target and released.
subtasks.starts_when: The held object starts descending (or moving) onto its target.
subtasks.ends_when: The effector has released the object and leaves it.
subtasks.success_when: The object rests at the target as the task requires (e.g. stacked, upright, inside).
subtasks.confusions: Release not visible: unknown. Resting half off, on the wrong target or falling over: failure. Dropping from height onto the target is still place.

subtasks.label: retreat
subtasks.definition: After releasing an object, the empty effector withdraws from it (or returns to rest).
subtasks.starts_when: The effector opens / lets go of the object it placed.
subtasks.ends_when: The effector has cleared the object, or starts toward the next object.
subtasks.success_when: The placed object is not disturbed.
subtasks.confusions: Only after place (or another release on a target); moving away after a failed grasp is approach toward the next contact.

subtasks.label: push
subtasks.definition: The effector moves an object by pushing it along its support without holding it.
subtasks.starts_when: The effector first contacts the object and it starts moving away from the effector.
subtasks.ends_when: The effector stops pushing (contact ends or the object stops).
subtasks.success_when: The object ends where the task wants it.
subtasks.confusions: Sliding an object while holding it is transport. Pressing without displacement is press.

subtasks.label: pull
subtasks.definition: The effector draws an object (or part of one) toward itself along a surface or an axis -- dragging, or pulling a handle, cable or rope.
subtasks.starts_when: The object first moves toward the effector under its pull.
subtasks.ends_when: The pull stops.
subtasks.success_when: The object or part ends where the task wants it.
subtasks.confusions: Pulling a drawer or door open is open.

subtasks.label: open
subtasks.definition: An articulated or covering part is opened: drawer, door, lid, cap, box flap, zipper, faucet valve.
subtasks.starts_when: The part first moves in its opening direction.
subtasks.ends_when: The part stops moving open (or the effector lets go of it).
subtasks.success_when: The part is open as far as the task needs.
subtasks.confusions: Reaching and taking hold of the handle before it moves is approach and grasp.

subtasks.label: close
subtasks.definition: An articulated or covering part is closed: drawer, door, lid, cap, box flap, zipper, faucet valve.
subtasks.starts_when: The part first moves in its closing direction.
subtasks.ends_when: The part stops moving closed (or the effector lets go of it).
subtasks.success_when: The part is fully closed.
subtasks.confusions: Putting a loose lid onto a container is place; closing a hinged lid is close.

subtasks.label: rotate
subtasks.definition: An object or a part (knob, dial, valve, handle, cap) is turned about an axis in place.
subtasks.starts_when: The object or part first turns.
subtasks.ends_when: It stops turning.
subtasks.success_when: It reaches the orientation or setting the task wants.
subtasks.confusions: Unscrewing or screwing a cap on a thread is screw. Turning an object over to rest on another face is reorient.

subtasks.label: screw
subtasks.definition: A threaded part (cap, bolt, bulb, screw) is screwed in or out.
subtasks.starts_when: The threaded part first turns on its thread.
subtasks.ends_when: It stops turning (tight, or free of the thread).
subtasks.success_when: It is fully tightened, or fully free.
subtasks.confusions: Lifting the freed cap away is transport.

subtasks.label: press
subtasks.definition: The effector presses a button, switch, key or surface to actuate it, without moving it along the surface.
subtasks.starts_when: The effector first touches the button or switch.
subtasks.ends_when: The effector leaves it.
subtasks.success_when: The device visibly actuates (light, state change) or the task's evidence shows it.
subtasks.confusions: Toggling a lever switch sideways is still press. Holding an object down so another action can happen is hold.

subtasks.label: insert
subtasks.definition: A held object is fitted into a close-fitting opening: slot, hole, socket, sleeve, container mouth.
subtasks.starts_when: The object first enters the opening.
subtasks.ends_when: The object is seated (or the effector releases it inside).
subtasks.success_when: The object is fully seated.
subtasks.confusions: Dropping an object into an open container is place.

subtasks.label: remove
subtasks.definition: A held object is extracted from where it is fitted or contained: slot, socket, holder, container, peg.
subtasks.starts_when: The held object first moves out of its fit.
subtasks.ends_when: It is free of the fit.
subtasks.success_when: It is fully out.
subtasks.confusions: Lifting a loose object off a surface is grasp then transport.

subtasks.label: pour
subtasks.definition: A held container is tilted so its contents flow out into or onto a target.
subtasks.starts_when: The held container starts tilting toward the target.
subtasks.ends_when: It is tilted back upright (or contents stop flowing).
subtasks.success_when: The contents land in the target.
subtasks.confusions: Carrying the container to the target is transport.

subtasks.label: scoop
subtasks.definition: A tool (spoon, spatula, scoop, ladle) collects material from a container or surface.
subtasks.starts_when: The tool first enters the material.
subtasks.ends_when: The tool leaves the material, loaded.
subtasks.success_when: The tool carries material out.

subtasks.label: stir
subtasks.definition: A tool or held object is moved repeatedly inside a container to mix its contents.
subtasks.starts_when: The tool first moves inside the contents.
subtasks.ends_when: The mixing motion stops.
subtasks.success_when: The motion covers the contents as the task asks.

subtasks.label: cut
subtasks.definition: A blade or cutting tool separates material.
subtasks.starts_when: The blade first contacts the material.
subtasks.ends_when: The blade leaves the material.
subtasks.success_when: The material is cut through as the task asks.

subtasks.label: wipe
subtasks.definition: A held cloth, sponge, brush or tool is moved across a surface in contact with it -- wiping, scrubbing, brushing, sweeping.
subtasks.starts_when: The held item first moves across the surface in contact.
subtasks.ends_when: It leaves the surface or the stroke motion stops.
subtasks.success_when: The target area is covered (or visibly cleaned).

subtasks.label: fold
subtasks.definition: A deformable object (cloth, towel, paper, bag, cable) is folded, unfolded, spread, rolled or draped.
subtasks.starts_when: The held part of the deformable object first moves in the folding (or spreading) motion.
subtasks.ends_when: The effector releases the moved part.
subtasks.success_when: The object has the shape the task asks for.
subtasks.confusions: Picking up a folded cloth and moving it elsewhere is grasp, transport, place.

subtasks.label: reorient
subtasks.definition: An object is turned over or set upright -- flipped onto another face, stood up, laid down -- with or without being lifted clear.
subtasks.starts_when: The object starts tipping or turning onto another face.
subtasks.ends_when: It rests on its new face.
subtasks.success_when: It rests in the orientation the task wants.
subtasks.confusions: Turning a knob or cap in place is rotate or screw.

subtasks.label: hold
subtasks.definition: The effector keeps an object still -- steadying it, pinning it or presenting it -- while something else happens.
subtasks.starts_when: The held object stops moving and is kept in place.
subtasks.ends_when: The effector moves it again or lets go.
subtasks.success_when: The object stays put for as long as the task needs.
subtasks.confusions: A pause with nothing held is other.

subtasks.label: handover
subtasks.definition: An object passes from one effector (or hand) to another.
subtasks.starts_when: The receiving effector first touches the object while the giver still holds it.
subtasks.ends_when: The giving effector has released it.
subtasks.success_when: The receiver holds the object alone.
